channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7367 vs. 6.7351 previous
item.description: On Thursday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7367 compared to last Wednesday's fix of 6.7351 and 6.7254 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Canadian Dollar hangs near April 2025 lows as USD sticks to bullish tone amid hawkish Fed
item.description: The USD/CAD pair retains its bullish undertone on Thursday, trading around the 1.4265 region during the Asian session, well within striking distance of the highest level since April 2025, touched earlier this week.

item.title: WTI posts modest gains above $88.50 on unexpected EIA draw, Middle East conflicts in focus
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $88.55 during the early Asian trading hours on Thursday. WTI posts modest gains as US crude oil inventories fell unexpectedly last week.

item.title: Pentagon orders readiness for potential Iran strikes as Trump weighs timing
item.description: The Pentagon told US Central Command (CENTCOM) several days ago to conclude preparations for resuming major combat operations in Iran, Axios reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Gold falls to two‑month low near $4,100 on stronger US Dollar
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to a near two-month low around $4,110 during the early Asian session on Thursday. A stronger US Dollar (USD) and elevated US Treasury bond yields reduce the appeal of the non-yielding metal.

item.title: The Yen round-trips after Japanese pay beats its forecast
item.description: Japanese pay grew faster than forecast in August and the Yen weakened anyway. USD/JPY trades near 158.00, back where it was before the release took it to its highest since September 25.

item.title: Australian Dollar slips as Fed hike bets meet Middle East Oil risk
item.description: The Australian Dollar makes a U-turn and loses over 0.29% on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve revealed members expect another rate hike towards the year-end. The AUD/USD trades at 0.6963.

item.title: The Euro gives back its bounce as French bonds sell off again
item.description: Banque de France Governor Moulin said on Wednesday that the strain in French bonds is serious but doesn't meet the conditions for help from the European Central Bank (ECB). French 10-year yields went back up after Tuesday's relief.

item.title: The Pound slides back to the bottom of its range as the bond selloff resumes
item.description: The low of every session since September 24 has come within half a cent of 1.3200, and Wednesday made it ten in a row. GBP/USD trades just above 1.3200, below the level Tuesday's rally started from.

item.title: Mexican Peso holds firm as FOMC Minutes signal further rate hikes
item.description: The Mexican Peso finishes its winning streak yet holds firm at around Wednesday’s opening price against the US Dollar, after the minutes of the Federal Reserve’s last meeting revealed that officials expect another rate hike by the year’s end. The USD/MXN trades at 17.98, virtually unchanged.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Tight ranges persist against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann describe USD/CNH as confined to a narrow intraday band around 6.7000, with a slightly firmer tone in the very short term.

item.title: Vietnamese Dong: Constructive but upside constrained – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Asia FX team highlights a constructive near-term outlook for the Vietnamese Dong (VND), supported by strong Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows and robust growth. USD/VND stayed around 25,994, below its July peak, leaving VND about 1.2% stronger year-to-date.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD cracks $60 as bears eye $56
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price extends its losses on Wednesday, following Gold’s path, as the latest Federal Reserve (Fed) Minutes showed that officials expect another rate increase towards the year-end. The XAG/USD pair trades at $59.69, down by over 1.67%.

item.title: South Korean Won: Upside risks with key levels in focus against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: Christopher Wong at OCBC Bank notes that USD/KRW continues to trade heavy as exporter US Dollar (USD) selling and a softer external backdrop support the Korean Won (KRW), even as foreign equity outflows cap gains.

item.title: Gold slides below $4,100 as FOMC Minutes signal further Fed hikes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price pressures on the downside on Wednesday, yet it has reclaimed the $4,100 mark as US Treasury yields erased some of its earlier gains and turned negative.

item.title: Thai Baht: Inflation rise and THB downside risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank economists note Thailand’s September CPI rose 2.8% year-on-year, below consensus but the highest since April, bringing headline inflation close to the upper end of the Bank of Thailand’s target range. They expect headline inflation to rise further on persistent supply-side pressures, yet see demand-side forces as benign. USD/THB fell to 33.62, though downside risks to the Baht remain elevated.

item.title: Fed Minutes: Officials saw inflation risks worsening before September hike
item.description: All participants at the Federal Reserve's (Fed) September 15–16 meeting supported the 25-basis-point rate increase, while most judged that another hike would probably be appropriate by the end of the year.

item.title: Forex Today: Weekly Claims and Fedspeak on top of the agenda
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has resumed its uptrend, advancing to two-day highs while rapidly forgetting Tuesday’s hiccup. The extra gains in the Greenback have come in tandem with the equally decent advance in US Treasury yields on the belly and long end of the curve.

item.title: China: Targeted stimulus supports growth – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategist Michelle Lam analyzes recent Chinese policy moves, noting that new property and monetary easing should keep growth on track and help China meet its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) target at the lower end of the range.

item.title: WTI reverses earlier gains as recovering Middle East exports weigh
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil trades lower on Wednesday, giving up earlier gains as a stronger US Dollar (USD) and recovering Middle East exports offset support from an unexpected decline in US crude inventories.

item.title: Thailand: BoT policy risks balanced – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economist Tim Leelahaphan expects the Bank of Thailand (BoT) to keep its policy rate at 1.0% through 2026 and 2027, with the BoT prioritising economic growth over inflation. He highlights asymmetric risks around this on-hold call, noting that any hikes would likely be gradual while cuts could be faster if domestic growth slows sharply.

item.title: British Pound buckles as 30-year Gilts top 6%, US yields soar
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) dives over 0.48% against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as US Treasury yields hit a 24-year high, boosting the Greenback’s appeal, while traders await the release of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) last meeting minutes.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Pair consolidates below key moving averages
item.description: USD/JPY trades in a narrow range on Wednesday, with the Japanese Yen (JPY) holding a slight advantage over the US Dollar (USD) as traders assess hawkish Bank of Japan (BoJ) signals. Intervention risks near the 160.00 level also keep traders cautious.

item.title: Gold tests $4,100 as US Dollar and yields rise ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its decline on Wednesday, falling nearly 1.3% as the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields resume their advance following a modest pullback the previous day.

item.title: US Dollar Index climbs back near its 18-month high as yields rise
item.description: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note touched 5.35% on Wednesday, its highest since April 2002, and the 30-year bond hit a 24-year high. Brent is back above $100 a barrel after Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: NY Fed September survey shows households bracing for higher prices
item.description: The New York Fed's September Survey of Consumer Expectations showed that American households expect short-term inflation to rise, while in the long term, they expect prices to cool but remain above the Federal Reserve’s 2% goal.

item.title: IEA members back faster release of 100 million barrels of Oil stocks
item.description: Governments belonging to the International Energy Agency (IEA) support accelerating the release of Oil stocks announced under the collective action agreed in March, according to a statement from the organization cited by Reuters on Wednesday.

item.title: Vietnam: Strong GDP but rising inflation risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank Research highlights Vietnam’s Q3 GDP growth at 10.0% year-on-year, the strongest since the pandemic, driven by investment and industry. Achieving the government’s 10% full-year target would require an unusually strong Q4.

item.title: Euro struggles as French fiscal risks, strong US Dollar weigh ahead of Fed Minutes
item.description: EUR/USD extends its decline on Wednesday as the Euro (EUR) remains under broad selling pressure, while the US Dollar (USD) strengthens alongside surging US Treasury yields. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1195, down 0.57% on the day, hovering near its lowest level in 17 months.

item.title: US Treasury yields hit 24-year highs as 10-year tests 5.35%
item.description: US Treasury yields soar on Wednesday, with the 10- and 30-year yields reaching 24-year highs of 5.35% and 5.724%, respectively, suggesting that investors are demanding a higher premium on US debt amid inflation and fiscal policy concerns.
